observations.text: At review entry, the detached checkout HEAD matched PRAXIS_TASK_COMMIT and the worktree was clean; the Praxis repository, issue, branch, and task path were present.
The capture code creates the protocol ledger after identity/resource validation and fresh preflight; a campaign claim and attempt claims are then written under the ledger.
write_new flushes and fsyncs claim file contents, while the ledger creation/write path has no directory fsync; EvidenceRun syncs the capture output directory separately.

The per-case deadline wraps episode execution; model/policy setup precedes it and analysis follows it. The offline verifier checks prepared/capture references, authorization, preflight, ledger claims, trace replay, and repeat semantics.
The review JSON targets the frozen starting commit and is the only path in the result commit; the worktree is clean after commit.

inferences.text: Because the START record is not consumed before preflight and ledger creation, an invocation that fails earlier can be re-entered with the same authorization and later consume campaign attempts, contrary to the exact-once task rule.
Without syncing ledger directory entries, a host/filesystem crash can leave claim contents fsynced but remove the names used to block a replacement campaign.
A stall in capture setup or post-episode analysis is outside the 300-second watchdog and can leave a claimed campaign without a bounded terminal result.

conclusions.text: The execution review verdict is VETO because exact-once/replacement-run prevention and crash-durable external claims are not sufficiently enforced; watchdog coverage also excludes capture setup and analysis.
No formal campaign result or scientific conclusion was produced by this review task.

uncertainty.text: Whether an unsynced directory entry is lost depends on filesystem and crash timing; this review made no crash-injection run, and the source does not guarantee persistence with directory fsync.

Offline performance verification recomputes most gate metrics through the capture analyzer and separately checks MAE only; common-mode mean-speed, lateral, and yaw calculation defects could pass that verifier.
